bodySections.heading: Why timing matters for this schedule
paragraphs: Plan Wire Fox Terrier social milestones around the schedule rows, not the other way around, because the 16-week finish is the usual green light clinics cite for broader Wire Fox Terrier exposure.
Weight range 15-20 lb (7-9 kg) and grooming needs (Wire coat strip.) belong in the same Wire Fox Terrier household ops list as vaccine dates when busy weeks collide.
If your Wire Fox Terrier is also monitored for eye lens luxation risk, ask whether bloodwork or orthopedic checks can share a visit with a booster to cut missed Wire Fox Terrier appointments.
After the Wire Fox Terrier puppy/kitten series, keep adult DA2PP / DHPP and rabies renewals on 7/3/1-day reminders so year-two surprises disappear.

bodySections.heading: If a dose is missed or delayed
paragraphs: Owners postpone Wire Fox Terrier shots when the puppy seems “a little off,” travel intervenes, or patellar luxation worries dominate the week — ask the clinic whether a same-week Wire Fox Terrier make-up is still appropriate instead of sliding to the annual exam.
Long gaps can leave Wire Fox Terrier antibody levels uncertain, so expect either an added booster or a titer conversation rather than a shrug.
Do not trade the missed Wire Fox Terrier dose for extra socialization; finish immunity first for this small dog.
Reset the Wire Fox Terrier reminder stack the evening of the make-up appointment — including the eventual adult booster after the 16-week finish.

faqs.question: When does the Wire Fox Terrier core vaccine series usually finish?
faqs.answer: This breed record completes core vaccines around 16 weeks of age, with rabies timed per local law. Your clinic may adjust intervals for the individual puppy.

faqs.question: What should I do if my Wire Fox Terrier misses a booster?
faqs.answer: Contact your veterinarian for a catch-up plan instead of restarting or skipping ahead. Keep prior dates handy and limit high-risk exposure until the series is current again.

faqs.question: Where can I read Wire Fox Terrier health context beyond vaccines?
faqs.answer: See the Wire Fox Terrier adult health guide for breed predispositions such as patellar luxation, then bring those notes to wellness and vaccine visits.
